extra.message: User-controlled input form['user_id'] (user_id_form) is concatenated into a raw SQL string via Python %-formatting and passed to User.objects.raw(). An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL through the POST 'user_id' field, allowing data exfiltration, authentication bypass, or privilege escalation (the ORDER BY is_admin clause even surfaces admin records).

hits_by_ip() builds a raw SQL command by %-formatting the 'ip' and 'col' arguments directly into the query string and executes it with cursor.execute(). Both values originate from attacker-controlled request.GET data in admin_analytics (app/views/admin/views.py:88-98: request.GET['ip'] and the GET dict keys forming 'col'), enabling SQL injection.

The 'class' query parameter (request.GET.get('class')) is passed directly to eval(). This is arbitrary Python code execution (RCE): an attacker can supply any expression as the 'class' value to execute code on the server.

cwe: CWE-95: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code (Eval Injection)

extra.message: The 'class' query parameter (request.GET.get('class')) is passed directly to eval() in api_id(). This allows arbitrary Python code execution (RCE) via the user-supplied 'class' value. This endpoint also lacks authentication.

extra.message: os.system() executes a shell command built from full_file_name and bak_file_path, both derived from the uploaded file's attacker-controlled name (orig_file.name / uploaded_file.name from request.FILES in upload view). A crafted filename containing shell metacharacters results in OS command injection / remote code execution.

reset_password() calls pickle.loads(base64.b64decode(request.POST['user'])) on attacker-controlled POST data with no integrity verification. Deserializing untrusted pickle data allows arbitrary code execution (RCE) on the server.

The download view builds a filesystem path by concatenating BASE_DIR with the unsanitized 'name' query parameter (request.GET.get('name')) and then opens/serves that file. An attacker can supply '../' sequences (e.g. ?name=../../etc/passwd) to read arbitrary files outside the intended directory (path traversal / arbitrary file read).

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory (Path Traversal)

extra.message: save_data() builds the destination path with os.path.join(data_path, uploaded_file.name) using the attacker-controlled uploaded filename and writes it via default_storage.save(). A filename containing '../' allows writing files outside MEDIA_ROOT/data (path traversal on upload), potentially overwriting application files.

extra.message: The login handler reads 'path' from request.POST (line 27) and passes it unvalidated to HttpResponseRedirect(path). An attacker can craft a login form/link with an external 'path' value to redirect the authenticated victim to an attacker-controlled site (open redirect), facilitating phishing/credential theft.

extra.message: safe_name() wraps the user-controlled first_name field in mark_safe(), disabling Django's automatic HTML escaping. Since first_name is set from unvalidated signup/update form input, rendering safe_name in a template results in stored cross-site scripting (XSS).

admin_update_user is protected only by @user_is_authenticated (any logged-in user) and performs no admin/ownership check before updating arbitrary users by selected_id. Any authenticated user can modify any other user's record (including via mass-assignment of POST data into update(**data)), an authorization bypass / privilege-escalation flaw. admin_delete_user, admin_get_user, admin_get_all_users and admin_analytics share the same missing-admin-authorization issue.

user_pay() deletes a Pay record by the pay_id taken directly from the URL without verifying that the record belongs to the currently authenticated user. Any authenticated user can delete any other user's direct-deposit/pay record (Insecure Direct Object Reference).

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: user_message() fetches and deletes a Message by message_id from the URL with no check that the message belongs to the current user. Any authenticated user can read or delete arbitrary messages by guessing/iterating message ids (IDOR).

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: check_if_valid_token() derives the user id from the client-supplied Authorization header and validates it with a weak regex 'group_id-group_hash' scheme over a SHA1(salt:group_id) hash. The group_id is fully attacker-controlled and the hash is computable by any client that knows/guesses the salt; combined with extrapolate_user() trusting the same header, this is a broken authentication mechanism allowing impersonation of arbitrary users (including admins at api_index).

User passwords are hashed and compared using unsalted MD5 (hashlib.md5). MD5 is cryptographically broken and unsalted, making stored password hashes trivially crackable via rainbow tables/brute force. Auth tokens (line 141) and reset tokens (password_resets) likewise rely on MD5.

cwe: CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm

extra.message: Django SECRET_KEY is hardcoded in source. Exposure of the secret key allows forging session cookies, CSRF tokens, and signed values, leading to authentication bypass and tampering.

A static AES encryption KEY is hardcoded in settings.py and used by Encryption.get_key() to encrypt/decrypt sensitive values (SSNs, bank account numbers). A hardcoded symmetric key compromises confidentiality of all encrypted PII. ACCESS_TOKEN_SALT (line 135) is similarly hardcoded.

DEBUG = True is enabled. In production this exposes detailed stack traces, settings, and source snippets to attackers on unhandled errors (information disclosure). Combined with ALLOWED_HOSTS = ['*'] (line 27), it also permits Host header attacks.
ALLOWED_HOSTS is set to ['*'], disabling Django's Host header validation. This enables Host header poisoning attacks (e.g. cache poisoning and password-reset link spoofing).
Database credentials (USER 'root' / PASSWORD 'password') are hardcoded in docker_settings.py. Hardcoded database credentials in source control expose the database if the repo is leaked.

AES-CBC is used with a per-user fixed IV (get_iv returns the stored KeyManagement.iv) and a single static key. Reusing the same key+IV across encryptions of sensitive PII (SSN, bank numbers) leaks plaintext equality and weakens CBC confidentiality.

cwe: CWE-329: Generation of Predictable IV with CBC Mode
